replies.user: [CURRICULUM: Unit 1, Lesson 1] Teach me what physically happens inside an LLM when I type a prompt. Start with tokenization and next-token prediction. After explaining, give me a hands-on exercise.
replies.raw:
Here's something that might surprise you: the word "bank" is the **same token** whether you're talking about a riverbank or a savings account.

The model doesn't know which meaning you intend just from the word itself — it has to figure that out from context.

That's the first puzzle of how LLMs work, and it starts before the model even "thinks."

---

When you type a prompt, the very first thing that happens is **tokenization** — your text gets chopped into chunks called tokens.

Tokens aren't exactly words. "Unbelievable" might be three tokens: "un", "believ", "able." A short common word like "the" is usually one token.

GPT-4's tokenizer has a vocabulary of about 100,000 possible tokens.

[EX]Type "I put cash in the bank." Each word (roughly) becomes a token. Then each token gets converted to a number — its ID in the vocabulary list. The model never sees letters. It only ever sees numbers.[/EX]

[KEY]Tokenization converts your text into a sequence of numbers before the model does anything else.[/KEY]

[Q]
What does a tokenizer actually hand off to the rest of the model?
A) The original words, spell-checked and cleaned up
B) A sequence of numbers representing chunks of text
C) A lookup table of dictionary definitions for each word
ANS: B
[/Q]

replies.user: [CURRICULUM: Unit 1, Lesson 1] Teach me what physically happens inside an LLM when I type a prompt. Start with tokenization and next-token prediction. After explaining, give me a hands-on exercise.
replies.raw:
Here's something that might surprise you: the word "bank" is always the same token — the same number — no matter what it means.

Whether you're writing about a riverbank or a savings account, the model sees identical input. It has to figure out the meaning from context alone.

That's the first thing happening the moment you hit send: your words get chopped into **tokens**.

A token is roughly a word or word-chunk — "running" might be one token, "un" + "believ" + "able" might be three. Each token gets converted to a number, and that number is its ID in the model's vocabulary.

GPT-4's tokenizer has a vocabulary of about 100,000 of these tokens.

[EX]Type "The cat sat on the mat" and the model doesn't see letters or words — it sees something like a short list of numbers, one per token.[/EX]

[KEY]Tokenization turns your text into a sequence of numbers before the model touches it at all.[/KEY]

[Q]
What does a tokenizer actually convert your words into?
A) A ranked list of possible meanings for each sentence
B) A sequence of numbers, one per token
C) A compressed audio file the model can process
ANS: B
[/Q]
